comp170.name: COMP 170 Introduction to Programming with Python
comp170.description: An introductory college programming course in Python, for students with little to no prior coding experience. Deliberately avoids heavy technical terminology, framing programming as problem-solving and common sense rather than jargon. Covers variables, control flow, functions, and basic data structures. The concept of an object -- essentially, a program bundled with its own data -- is introduced only near the end of the term.

comp271.name: COMP 271 Linear Data Structures
comp271.description: The course that follows COMP 170, in Python. It serves two purposes: first, to reinforce and advance the programming skills built in COMP 170; second, to work through basic algorithms for linear data structures such as dynamic arrays and linked lists. Because Python lists are already dynamically sized, arrays are deliberately treated as fixed-size in this course so students can learn how resizing actually works -- allocating a new array and moving contents over from the old one. The course also explores objects in more depth: design, field privacy, an exposed interface, abstract classes, and inheritance. Basic sorting (mergesort) is used as an entry point into discussing Big-Theta asymptotic behavior in general terms. Terminology grows more advanced than COMP 170, but the course still frames programming as problem-solving via common sense.

comp363.name: COMP 363 Design and Analysis of Algorithms
comp363.description: A more quantitatively oriented course in algorithm design and analysis. Topics include the Master Theorem for analyzing divide-and-conquer recurrences, graph algorithms and their Big-Theta behavior, dynamic programming, min-cut/max-flow, numerical methods and simulations, basic backpropagation, and predictive analytics applied to real-world datasets (e.g. sports data, police data).
